headline: Board approves septic variances for 2 Wallace Ct, six-month extension for 34 Marble Rd, water certificate for 3 Toronto Ave, and fine for Boulevard Variety tobacco violation.
summary: The Board of Health approved septic variance and relief requests for 2 Wallace Court, granted a six-month plan extension for 34 Marble Road, and accepted a water supply certificate for 3 Toronto Avenue noting elevated radon and sodium. The Board also heard a tobacco violation appeal from Boulevard Variety and voted to impose a fine, discussed tobacco compliance check results, a rental education project, and various health department updates including a kratom ban and moving future meetings to the second Thursday of the month.
decisions: Approved the August 6, 2026 Board of Health minutes as written, 3-0.
Approved the septic variance and relief requests for 2 Wallace Court, 3-0.
Granted a six-month extension for 34 Marble Road with no further extensions, 3-0.
Accepted the water supply certificate for 3 Toronto Avenue with a proviso noting elevated radon and sodium, 3-0.
Imposed a first nicotine and tobacco violation fine on Boulevard Variety, 3-0.
Agreed to move future Board of Health meetings to the second Thursday of the month starting in November.

plain_text:
CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
Board of Health 
Minutes of the Meeting 
September 4, 2026, 5:30 p.m. 
Harbormaster Conference Room & 
Hybrid Meeting Via Zoom 
 
Board members present: Chairperson: Joseph Rosa; Vice-Chairperson: Dr. Eric Kaplan; and 
Jesse Dole. Absent: Erin George and Thomas Markert.  
 
Also present: Health Director: Dominique Hurley; Assistant Health Director: Gabrielle White; 
Sanitarian: Cody Smith; Public Health Excellence Program Manager: Danielle Larabee; Senior 
Health Inspector: Brie Turko; Director of the North Shore Tobacco Control: Joyce Redford; 
Regional Prevention Director: Chelsea Goldstein-Walsh; and Advisor to the Septic Review 
Subcommittee: Dave Sargent. 
 
The meeting started at 5:30 p.m.  
 
Public Oral Communication 
  
There was no “Public Oral Communication”.  
 
Approval of Minutes 
                  
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan to approve the Gloucester Board of Health minutes for the meeting of 
August 6, 2026, as written. Seconded by Mr. Dole. Carried 3-0.  
2 Wallace Ct - Septic Relief Request - Designer: Dan Johnson-Domestic Septic Design 
○ Gloucester Onsite Wastewater Regulations Variance Request: reduction from the 
proposed leaching area to a public water supply from 400 feet to 368 feet, Table  
i. Request reduction from the proposed septic tank with pump vault to a 
public water supply from 400 feet to 309 feet, Table 1.  
ii. Request reduction from the proposed leaching area to a wetland 
bordering a public water supply from 400 feet to 168 feet, Table 1. 
iii. Request reduction from the proposed septic tank with pump vault to a 
public water supply from 400 feet to 79 feet, Table 1. 
○ Local Upgrade Approval Relief Request 
i. Request reduction for the offset from the septic tank with pump vault to 
the property line from 10 feet to 3 feet, 310 CMR 15.211 and 15.405 (1) 
(a). 
ii. Request reduction for the offset from the septic tank with pump vault to 
the house foundation from 10 feet to 8 feet, 310 CMR 15.211 and 
15.405(1) (b).
Page 2 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
Mr. Smith stated that 4 variances are before the Board for 2 Wallace Court. He gave a brief 
overview of the variance and relief requests. 
 
Dan Johnson, designer of Domestic Septic Design, appeared before the Board. He briefed the 
Board members on the property and the variance and relief requests.  
 
Mr. Sargent stated that the proposed system is much better than the existing system and will be 
regularly monitored. He stated that he doesn’t see any environmentally sensitive areas right 
next to the property that would be impacted, so doing something with denitrification really 
doesn't make sense. 
 
Mr. Smith stated that they went the extra step of making sure there was an RLS who surveyed 
the property to make sure that the property lines were correct. He stated that his 
recommendation is to grant the requests.  
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak for or against the request 
for relief or the variances. There was no one.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Dole that the Board of Health approve the requests for relief and the variances 
requested as outlined on the agenda for 2 Wallace Court. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. Carried 3-
0. 
34 Marble Rd. - Plan Extension-Requesting an Additional One-Year Extension Beyond the 
2025 Extension Granted for the Plan Approved in 2015- 
Mr. Smith stated that the plan that was approved in 2015 was for two lots, 34 Marble Road and 
then across the street at 29 Marble Road. He stated that one property was a three-bedroom 
house and the other property was a 1-bedroom house. He stated that the Health Department 
issued a plan extension last year that gave the applicant an additional year, so they have until 
November 1st, 2026, to build a system. He stated that the plan approval does say at the bottom 
that no plan extension will be given beyond the November 1st, 2026, deadline. He stated that 
the request for a plan extension came in uniquely before the new regulations went into effect, 
and the new regulations state that applicants are only allowed one plan extension. He stated 
that the construction of this system exceeds $200,000, so the owner is looking at potentially 
trying to connect to the sewer line as a possible alternative.  
 
Barney Lichtenstein, owner of 34 Marble Road, appeared before the Board. He stated that there 
were a lot of circumstances that were unusual with this situation. He stated that for years Max 
Schenk repeatedly told him that he did not have to do anything to renew this system. He gave 
an overview of the delays he has encountered. He stated that because of the high cost of the 
system, he would like to connect to city sewer if possible. He stated that his designer, Dan 
Ottenheimer, did not let him know anything about the plans that were registered with the Health 
Department until this past April.
Page 3 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
Ms. Hurley noted that the City isn't responsible if his designer failed to make the owner aware of 
the plans that were registered. She confirmed that Max Schenk was right about renewal at the 
time, as the old regulations allowed it, while the new ones do not. She stated that the Health 
Department wrote a letter last year that said no more extensions without a full plan, and that is 
what is before the Board right now.   
 
Mr. Sargent stated that because ledge is undulating in the area that may be costly and 
prohibitive for a sewer line going through that area.  
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak for or against the request 
for an extension. There was no one. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Dole that the Board of Health grant the request for a six-month extension for 34 
Marble Road with absolutely no further extensions beyond that. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. 
Carried 3-0. 
3 Toronto Ave. - Water Supply Certificate- 
Mr. Smith gave a brief overview of the water supply certificate. He stated that they had a well 
drilled in 2018, when they were under construction for their new home. He stated that they are 
attempting to get a water well certificate now because they need it as part of the sale of their 
property, and they have met all of the current regulation requirements except for the water 
analysis. He stated that the water well analysis for sodium was 57 milligrams per liter, and the 
State and the Health Department’s regulation only allows for 20 milligrams per liter. He stated 
that the other contaminant that was high for this well was radon. 
 
Chairperson Rosa stated that the sodium exceedance is not much of a concern since their local 
water is nearly 57 milligrams per liter, but the radon has no federal or state limits, and radon can 
cause various cancers and neurological problems. Because of Gloucester’s geology, the 
potential for radon contamination exists for any water sourced from wells throughout Cape Ann. 
He stated that the public should be aware that tests are available and there exist established 
methods for remediation.  
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak for or against the water 
certificate. There was no one.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Rosa that the Board of Health accept the water certificate for 3 Toronto Avenue 
with the proviso that the certificate mentions that the well has been tested and had elevated 
levels of radon and sodium. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. Carried 3-0.  
 
Nicotine and Tobacco Violations Briefing-  
Ms. Turko stated that on August 19, 2026, the North Shore/Cape Ann Tobacco Policy Program 
conducted tobacco compliance checks at 29 permitted tobacco establishments in Gloucester,
Page 4 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
with participation from two underage youth. She stated that the compliance checks identified 9 
violations at 8 establishments. She stated that 2 were sales to a minor violations and 7 were 
flavored tobacco violations. She stated that on July 29, 2026, the North Shore/Cape Ann 
Tobacco Policy Program and Ms. Hurley conducted an inspection of Sunny Variety. She stated 
that the inspection identified three violations. She stated that the violations were for tobacco 
products observed on the counter, flavored tobacco products or flavor enhancers observed and 
available for sale, and the Board of Health and Department of Revenue permits were not 
observed posted as required. 
Ms. Hurley stated that following the issuance of the tobacco violation letters sent to the 
establishments on August 21, 2026, the Health Department was made aware of errors in some 
of the order letters. She stated the Health Department is currently rewriting and reissuing 
corrected violation orders, as appropriate. She stated that the number of appeals currently 
requested may decrease once the corrected orders are issued and reviewed by the affected 
establishments. She stated that the Health Department requested additional information from 
some establishments regarding the specific grounds for their appeals. The appeals are currently 
scheduled to be heard at the October 1, 2026 Board of Health meeting. 
 
Ms. Hurley suggested that the Board consider updating its local regulations to more explicitly 
require that retailers comply with federal, state, and local law. She suggested that they amend 
the regulation to require that the retailer demonstrate attention to federal law as part of their 
application process, and they could accomplish this by having the retailer submit inventory 
reports with documentation and attestation showing how they are compliant with federal, state, 
and local law, with that inventory list. The board discussed amending the regulation to explicitly 
condition it upon compliance with state, local, and federal law. 
 
Ms. Redford gave an overview of the flavored tobacco ban. She stated that the FDA recently 
announced plans to notify 300,000 retailers that they cannot sell products without a Marketing 
Granted Order (MGO), which proves the FDA authorized the product for sale in the U.S.  
 
Nicotine and Tobacco Violation Appeal: Boulevard Variety-  
 
Joseph Youssef, owner of Boulevard Variety, at 33 Western Avenue, appeared before the 
Board. He stated that he became the owner of the establishment on January 21, 2026, and 
asked the Board to consider his status as a new owner. He requested that the Board take mercy 
and consideration of the violation, as this is his first violation as the new owner. He stated that 
he has implemented measures to prevent future violations, including the use of a scanner to 
verify identification for customers purchasing cigarettes and tobacco products. He reported that 
he and his employees have actively confiscated more than 40 suspected fake IDs and provided 
them to the Gloucester Police Department. He requested that the Board accept his appeal and 
consider the video documentation that he provided. He expressed his commitment to the 
Gloucester community and his desire to operate his business in compliance with the 
regulations.
Page 5 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
Ms. Turko stated that she was unaware that he was a new owner, so it actually came up as a 
second violation because there was a previous compliance issue within the last 36 months for 
Boulevard Variety.  
 
Ms. Redford stated that she and Ms. Hurley visited the store on July 29th, 2026, and found ZYN 
Chill, a flavored product, on their shelf. She stated that they asked them to remove the product, 
and when they returned on August 19th, 2026, a minor was able to buy the same product that 
they were asked to remove.    
 
Chairperson Rosa stated that he would like to organize mandatory training sessions for 
retailers, similar to what Peabody has done successfully with 40+ retailers across multiple 
sessions. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Rosa that the Board of Health impose a first nicotine and tobacco violation fine 
for Boulevard Variety. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. Carried 3-0.  
Rental Education Project- 
Ms. Hurley stated that the Rental Education Project builds on the goals established through the 
Rental Registration Program and supports the Department’s FY2027 objective to expand 
landlord services and launch tenant rights and obligations education to improve housing 
compliance and encourage safe living conditions. She stated that these efforts provide an 
opportunity to strengthen their approach to rental housing by pairing regulatory requirements 
with education, communication, and practical resources.  
 
Ms. Turko stated that they have been developing a rental education project to create a more 
strategic approach rather than just simply create materials and distribute information. She stated 
that the campaign is designed to support meaningful behavior change among both landlords 
and tenants. She stated that it begins by identifying current behaviors and defining the desired 
behaviors needed to promote safe, healthy, and well-maintained housing. She stated that these 
desired behaviors inform specific objectives, strategies, and tactics, creating a framework for 
ensuring that their education and outreach efforts are purposeful, consistent, and aligned with 
public health goals. She stated that at this stage, the Health Department is focusing on two 
priority tactics: the Tenant Resource Kit and the Housing Newsletter. She stated that the Tenant 
Resource Kit will provide tenants with accessible information about their rights, responsibilities, 
complaint resolution, communication, and available resources and the Housing Newsletter will 
provide ongoing education and reinforcement for landlords and tenants, with practical 
information about housing requirements, shared responsibilities, common issues, solutions, and 
available resources. She shared a flowchart that demonstrates the strategic connection 
between current behaviors, desired behavior changes, objectives, strategies, and tactics. She 
stated that as the project moves into implementation, they will establish measurable indicators 
to assess reach, engagement, knowledge, and behavior change, as well as longer-term 
indicators of improved housing compliance and safer living conditions. She stated that they also 
discussed conducting landlord and tenant focus groups to gather direct feedback from the
Page 6 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
people. She stated that they are also going to establish symmetrical indicators to evaluate 
whether their efforts are reaching landlords and tenants. 
 
Chairperson Rosa asked about the participation of the rental registry. Ms. Turko responded that 
they have a little over 400 people who are currently not renewed, so they will be sending out 
noncompliance letters to get them renewed. She stated that renewals are going to be 
happening in January, so they need everyone renewed for 2026 by November. 
 
Ms. Hurley commended Ms. Turko on her work on the Rental Education Project.   
 
Health Director’s Recap 
Presented by Dominique Hurley 
 
Ms. Hurley briefed the Board on the kratom ban the Governor just announced. She stated that 
kratom is now classified as a Schedule 1 drug. She stated that they just sent out cease and 
desist letters to retailers regarding kratom products, following DPH guidelines and legal review. 
She stated that those products have to get off the shelf and the State has given them a path to 
complete that.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the Eastern Waste Transfer Station subcommittee will meet on 
September 9th. She stated that she will give an update at the October Board meeting, 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that at the last Board meeting they discussed updating the Nicotine and 
Tobacco Regulations. She stated that the Health Department has drafted an update and is 
waiting for the Legal Department to review it. She stated that they should have a draft ready at 
the October Board meeting.  
 
Ms. Hurley proposed moving board meetings from the first Thursday to the second Thursday of 
each month to allow more time for preparing volumetrics reports. The Board agreed to hold 
Board of Health meetings on the second Thursday of the month starting in November.  
 
Public Health Excellence (PHE) Grant - 
 
Ms. Larabee gave Board members a brief overview of the projects that she is managing with 
Gloucester and Manchester under the Public Health Excellence Grant. She stated that one 
project is file digitization, with the hope to eventually have a public portal where people can go in 
and pull their septic records, hazardous waste records, well records, and then in the future, 
potentially more. She stated that another project is the septic compliance software on which Mr. 
Williamson and Mr. Smith have been working really hard. She stated that this allows all of the 
pumpers and haulers to submit their O&M reports and pump reports in the field. She stated that 
the third project involves Berger Food Safety Consulting, which started two weeks ago to help 
with the summer surge of food inspections, with weekly reports being provided and Ms. Vorias 
handling reinspections. She reviewed a strategic assessment project led by Aldrich Tobin 
Partners focusing on health and human services needs in both Manchester and Gloucester, 
with data collection underway and recommendations expected in early fall.
Page 7 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
Ms. Larabee presented the Public Health Advisory Board's prioritized list of health initiatives, 
with housing inspections, nuisance and air pollution, and food with cold storage facilities 
identified as high-priority areas requiring RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) 
assignments. She stated that she will send the list of priorities to the Board members for them to 
review.  
 
Prevention Team Reporting - 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that she is excited to have a full team back on staff. She stated that 
they have been really busy with the start of the school year, doing a lot of capacity building. She 
stated that they are doing outreach to strengthen and sustain their relationships with the 
Gloucester Public Schools, as well as recruit for new Gloucester Youth Leadership Council 
members at both the middle and high school level. She highlighted some of the events that they 
attended in August, such as Countdown to Kindergarten, Kops n Kids Youth Anglers, and the 
GYLC Open House at Cape Ann Lanes. She stated that they will be tabling at the Meet the 
Teacher nights at the middle and high school later this month. 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that she met with the superintendent today to reconnect with her 
and just really listen to what her priorities are, and to confirm that the Health Department is 
available to support the schools. 
 
Communicable Disease Reporting 
 
Ms. Hurley reported that there were 7 cases of West Nile virus reported in Essex. She stated 
that from their wastewater data, they can see that COVID cases are starting to increase. 
 
The Board discussed ongoing funding challenges with finalizing a contract for wastewater data 
services with Biobot.  
 
Regulatory Reporting 
 
Sanitarian -  
 
Mr. Smith stated that Carmody has been fully launched as of August 1, the official 
implementation date. He stated that they are currently in the hypercare phase, which includes 
working with IT to complete the backup tool and developing the process to automatically pull 
volumetric data from the system.
Page 8 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
September 3, 2026 
 
Concerns of the Board 
 
Next Regular Monthly Meeting Board of Health- The next regular Board of Health meeting is 
scheduled for Thursday, October 8, 2026 at 5:30 pm.  
 
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan to adjourn. 
Seconded by Mr. Dole. CARRIED. 
MEETING ADJOURNED – 8:30 p.m. 
  
Respectfully submitted, 
________________________________ 
  
Bobbi Orlando 
  
Accepted by: 
  
_________________________________ 
  
Joe Rosa, Chairperson
